words.definition: to start doing a new hobby or activity
words.example: She has taken up the cello since she retired.

words.definition: to stop doing something, often because it is too difficult
words.example: He has given up the guitar after a few frustrating weeks.

words.definition: to try hard to do something
words.example: You need to make an effort if you want to improve quickly.

words.definition: to finally decide something, often after discussion
words.example: After a long meeting, the committee finally reached a decision.

words.definition: to do or say something to make people feel more relaxed in a social situation
words.example: The host told a joke to break the ice at the start of the party.
collocations: break the ice with a joke

words.example: She called me out of the blue after years of silence.

words.definition: despite what has just been said; however
words.example: The weather was terrible; nevertheless, they went ahead with the picnic.
He practised every day; as a result, his playing improved quickly.

words.definition: without being affected by; in spite of
words.example: Despite the rain, the match continued.

words.definition: able to be trusted to do what is expected
words.example: My neighbour is very reliable and always waters my plants when I'm away.

words.definition: the quality of being willing to give money, time or help freely
words.example: His generosity surprised everyone at the fundraiser.

words.definition: slowly, over a period of time
words.example: Her confidence gradually improved after a few lessons.
